genius.headline: Stanford's Karl Deisseroth shares the 2026 Nobel Prize in medicine for optogenetics
genius.summary: Karl Deisseroth, a Stanford University and Howard Hughes Medical Institute professor, was named on Oct. 5 as a joint winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Germany's Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. Deisseroth put the gene for a light-sensitive algae protein into rodent neurons, making it possible to switch specific brain cells on and off with light. The technique, known as optogenetics, is now widely used to study how the brain works.

facepalm.headline: Maricopa County's vendor mails 3,126 early ballots six days before the scheduled mailing date
facepalm.summary: Runbeck Election Services, the vendor Maricopa County, Ariz., uses to mail early ballots, sent 3,126 ballots to the Postal Service on Oct. 1, six days before the scheduled Oct. 7 mailing, according to the county recorder's office. The office said it had not authorized the early mailing and only learned of it afterward. County officials said the ballots went to the correct voters and remain valid.
